mission_1.search:
BFS: plan length = 13.5 , node counts = 928
A*:  plan length =  13.5 , node counts = 700
Both path lengths are equal and optimal (detected: 13.5m , optimal: 13.5m); however A* examined fewer cells (700 against 928)
BFS uses a queue and processes cells in FIFO order (frontier.popleft()). So, it expands cells in order of distance from the start, spreading out evenly in every direction until it reaches the goal.
A* uses a heap, which means it picks up the minimum value (smallest g+ctx.heuristics(cell)), so cells moving toward the goal come out first. That's why it examined fewer cells.
mission_1.failure:
On the open map, DFS path length is 111,, while BFS is much smaller, 13.5m. That is because BFS goes in breadth and expands cells in order of distance from the start (so, it gives us a shortest path). DFS goes in depth and check the newest cell first, so it provides us with one of the possible path and not necessarily optimal solution.
On the reachable map, all 4 planners reported no_path, which means the algorithm was executed, but the path simple doesn't exist. resource_limit means the runner stopped the search (time out and memory exceeds), but it doesn't necessarily mean that the path doesn't exist.
I used AI to write all four planners and checked the code myself by reading each function against the handout steps.
